summary: Reviewed units 93-138 (46 units, ~25 text_flags). Structure, split and translations are mostly faithful. Real errors: Hindi 'और' for vā in 104; Hindi unclear-word garble in 130 (samarātra split around the mark); Hindi viśeṣa mismatch in 133; missing Hindi unclear mark for mālā in 108; 'anyatamā' mistranslated as 'other' in 122; the conjectural verb utpādayet in 122 makes poor sense for a just-born child (upācaret/upapādayet likelier). Most other issues are minor: Hindi lacks the identifications and hedges the English has (owner policy), gender labels on adjectives of unstated nouns, dropped 'ca' (100, 125), supplied '(it)/(drugs)', and unflagged joined words. Hindi was machine-checked: no Latin letters and no brackets in any unit; no bare कषाय. Identifications: none judged wrong; hastiparṇī and barhiṣa stay unidentified; viḍa could be viḍa-lavaṇa (a prepared salt) but is left as drug name per glossary. Hardest ones (upakuñcikā, dhāmārgava, rohiṇī, mahāvṛkṣa, priyaṅgu, aṃśumatī pair) are correctly hedged. Regroup suggestion: 136+137 form one śloka (16+16 syllables); 102 appears to continue 103; 109 protasis with 110; 118 with 119. Units needing human decision: 93 (tālī/sa-kalkam), 97 (alarka), 111 (elā-pratīvāpa), 112 (muṣkaka), 115 (position of vā), 122 (verb), 133 (compound), 130 (samarātra), 132 (ucchādana).
glossary_suggestions: '(her)', '(it)', '(ones)': ruling suggested. A parenthesised pronoun for an unstated object is allowed in English only when the referent is certain from the surrounding units (the sūtikā in 130 and 132, from 124-125 and 133 'tāṃ'); otherwise omit it (107, 108: object uncertain). Hindi never takes the pronoun. Stated pronouns (enām in 101, tām in 133) are translated plainly without brackets.
picu = cotton wad (pledget); yavāgū = gruel (not 'thick gruel' where the text says dravā).

Hindi gloss forms for this chapter: प्रतीवाप यानी मिलाई जाने वाली वस्तु; कटु तेल यानी सम्भवतः सरसों का तेल; यमक यानी सम्भवतः तेल और घी का मिश्रण; यवक्षार यानी सम्भवतः यव की राख से बना अशुद्ध पोटैशियम कार्बोनेट; उत्तरबस्ति यानी मूत्रमार्ग या गर्भाशय में दी जाने वाली बस्ति; अनुवासन यानी तेल की बस्ति; बला यानी सम्भवतः बरियार; लाङ्गली यानी सम्भवतः कलिहारी; जीमूतक यानी सम्भवतः देवदाली; उशीर यानी खस; प्रियङ्गु यानी सम्भवतः फूलप्रियंगु; आर्तव यानी रज.
An unrestorable printed word is written in Hindi as one unit 'अस्पष्ट शब्द X' (X the whole printed word); never insert the mark inside the word (see 130).
hrasva/laghu pañcamūla = śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, bṛhatī, kaṇṭakārī, gokṣura (standard); pañcakola = long pepper, its root, cavya, citraka, dry ginger (standard).
'X ādi' as a drug group: English 'the group beginning with X' (a supplied 'group'); accepted for vatsakādi, varaṇādi, vīratarādi but consider 'X and the rest' if the owner wants zero supplied nouns.
viḍa: probably viḍa-lavaṇa (a prepared salt), disputed; keep 'drug name' until the owner decides.
Joined words printed without sandhi (vā, ca, vidhinā next to a previous word) are flagged once per unit as 'possible: printed joined'.
